detail.longDescription: I want to make a one time pad in Python. This example I found on Stack Overflow: def encrypt(pad, secret): return ''.join([chr(ord(c) ^ ord(secret[i])) for i, c in enumerate(pad[:len(secret)])]) I need to write the cipher (what the above function returns) either to a file or TCP/IP connection. When I tried to write the cipher to a file, I got: UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters in position 6-7: character maps to <undefined> How do I write the cipher to a file or socket with socket.sendall(...) ? EDIT I try to use this : def one_time_pad_encode(message: str, key: bytes) -> bytes: return bytes(p ^ s for p, s in zip(message.encode()[: len(key)], key)) def one_time_pad_decode(cipher: bytes, key: bytes) -> str: return bytes(p ^ s for p, s in zip(cipher, key)).decode() from below answer. I use then the code import secrets, random, string msg = "Hello World !" key = secrets.token_bytes(len(msg)) # First key key = ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, k= len(msg))).encode() # Second key print(msg) print(key) cipher = one_time_pad_encode(msg, key) print(cipher) msg2 = one_time_pad_decode(cipher, key) print(msg2) This works correctly, however if I use for example : msg = "Hello World !é" I get the error UnicodeDecodeError 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xc3 in position 13: unexpected end of data with either first ot second key generation type. Furthermore, if I try : msg = "Hello World !ée" It works again with either firt or second key generation type. However, the message returned by the decode function is Hello World :é , it lacks the last character ! There is something I do not understand with Unicode Character, if there are accentuated characters in the message, or special character "€", the returned message is truncated, e.g. for "Hello World ééààà !{}]e" I am returned "Hello World ééààà" . Could you help me in making the above code more robust with respect to unicode characters ? Solution Core functions : def one_time_pad_encode(message: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes: return bytes(p ^ s for p, s in zip(message[: len(key)], key)) def one_time_pad_decode(cipher: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes: return bytes(p ^ s for p, s in zip(cipher, key)) Test : import secrets msg = "Hello World ! Héhé €€" bmsg = msg.encode("utf-8") key = secrets.token_bytes(len(bmsg)) print(msg) print(bmsg) print(key) cipher = one_time_pad_encode(bmsg, key) print(cipher) bmsg2 = one_time_pad_decode(cipher, key) msg2 = bmsg2.decode("utf-8") print(msg2) which results into : Hello World !
